claims.text: Rapid high-temperature homogenization annealing will eliminate incipient Cr/V segregation in W38Ta36Cr15V11.
Local Cr/V segregation acts as the nucleation seed for radiation-induced precipitation.
Homogenization will prevent precipitate formation during irradiation to approximately 8 dpa.
Homogenization will preserve negligible irradiation hardening.
The annealing treatment will make the alloy more suitable for practical bulk fabrication.
The starting alloy is nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11 and can be produced by magnetron sputtering.
The starting alloy exhibits Cr and V segregation at grain boundaries and triple junctions.
Irradiation causes the segregated Cr and V to form Cr/V-rich precipitates.
The unmodified alloy exhibits minimal irradiation hardening.
A single-step anneal can dissolve Cr/V segregation and produce a chemically uniform single-phase solid solution before consolidation.
The W38Ta36Cr15V11 system has previously been irradiated at 1073 K to doses up to 8 dpa.
Annealing will reduce solute segregation at grain boundaries and triple junctions.
Removing local Cr/V enrichment will prevent radiation-induced segregation from progressing to detectable second-phase precipitation.
A chemically uniform microstructure will preserve the alloy's defect-sink characteristics.
The alloy's defect-sink characteristics are responsible for negligible irradiation hardening.
At approximately 8 dpa, the homogenized alloy will have little to no Cr/V-rich precipitation relative to the unmodified alloy.
At approximately 8 dpa, the homogenized alloy will retain near-constant hardness.
The unmodified alloy contains Cr/V-rich precipitates after irradiation to approximately 8 dpa.
Near 1073 K and up to 8 dpa define the applicable irradiation boundary for the proposed behavior.
The homogenization anneal can be selected to avoid detrimental grain growth and retain the material's thermal stability.

contradictions.description: The starting and control material is described as an as-deposited sputtered nanocrystalline state, while the experiment calls both sets bulk alloys. If the control is consolidated into bulk, it is no longer strictly as-deposited; if it is not consolidated, the control differs from the treated sample in both annealing and sample form.
